Octa

Octa is a desktop app for opening, cleaning and querying data, whatever format it comes in. Parquet, CSV, Excel, a SQLite file, a PDF's tables, a mailbox, a live PostgreSQL database or a bucket on S3: Octa shows it in one fast table where you can search, edit, compare, analyse and run SQL on it, then save it back or convert it to another format.

It is a single native program for Linux, macOS and Windows that runs locally and needs no account. Its engine also works as a command-line tool and as an MCP server, so AI agents like Claude can use it too.

📚 Documentation: https://thorstenfoltz.github.io/octa/

What it does

  • Open files bigger than memory, password-protected files and archives, with tabs, tiling and a folder sidebar, plus views for raw text, JSON trees, maps and timelines.
  • Connect to S3, Azure, GCS, SFTP, WebDAV, twelve database engines and REST APIs.
  • Edit cells, rows and columns with undo, formulas and calculated columns, then clean duplicates, outliers, missing values and personal data.
  • Combine and compare tables: joins (fuzzy and spatial too), file and database diffs, schema drift, cell history in Git.
  • Analyse with summaries, pivots, correlations, time series, cohorts, charts, forecasts and HTML reports.
  • Query any open table with DuckDB SQL, or ask the built-in assistant, on a cloud model or offline with Ollama.
  • Save in the original format or convert to another one, and automate it all with recipes, the command line or the MCP server.

What it reads

Parquet, CSV/TSV, JSON and JSON Lines, Excel, ODS, Arrow, Avro, ORC, SQLite, DuckDB, GeoPackage, Microsoft Access, SAS, QlikView QVD, SPSS, Stata, R, HDF5, MATLAB, NetCDF, NumPy, MessagePack, BSON, DBF, XML, TOML, YAML, Jupyter notebooks, Markdown, HTML, EPUB, PDF tables, log files, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GPX, KML, Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Lance, fixed-width text, zip/tar archives, SQL dumps, email (.eml, .mbox, Outlook .msg, .pst, .olm), calendars and contacts, and source code. See supported formats for what each one can do, and samples/ for an example of each.

Installation

Building from source works on all three platforms: install Rust, clone this repository, and run cargo build --release. Linux and macOS need a few native libraries first, Windows needs a C++ toolchain; the installation guide lists them per platform, along with uninstall steps and the first-launch security prompts on Windows and macOS.

Linux (and WSL)

Install the latest release with one command, user-local (no sudo):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thorstenfoltz/octa/master/get-octa.sh | bash -s -- ~/.local

Or system-wide into /usr/local:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thorstenfoltz/octa/master/get-octa.sh | sudo bash

On WSL, also install a file dialog backend, or Open and Save as have nothing to show and appear to do nothing (Octa says so in the status bar):

sudo apt install xdg-desktop-portal-gtk   # or: sudo apt install zenity

An AppImage and a plain tarball are on the releases page. A downloaded AppImage still needs its execute bit, and a file manager will silently ignore a double-click until it has one:

chmod 750 Octa-*-x86_64.AppImage
./Octa-*-x86_64.AppImage

Arch Linux

On Arch and Arch-based distributions (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Garuda, ...) Octa is on the AUR, either built from source or as the prebuilt binary. Both install the man page, so man octa works:

Build from source:

paru -S octa

Or take the prebuilt binary:

paru -S octa-bin

Swap paru for yay or any other AUR helper you use.

macOS

One line, no password, Apple Silicon:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thorstenfoltz/octa/master/get-octa.sh | bash

It puts Octa.app into ~/Applications and octa into ~/.local/bin, and because curl marks nothing as quarantined, macOS opens it without a Gatekeeper warning. Intel Macs build from source.

The Octa.app bundle is also on the releases page. It is not notarised, so a copy downloaded with a browser makes macOS claim "the developer cannot be verified" (and occasionally that the app is damaged). Neither means anything is wrong with the download: how to open it anyway.

Windows

Install from the Microsoft Store: one click, no SmartScreen prompt, and the Store keeps it updated.

Or download octa.exe from the releases page and run it, no installation needed. install.ps1 (per-user, no admin) or install.bat (system-wide) set it up properly with a Start Menu entry.

Those downloads are not code-signed, so Windows shows "Windows protected your PC" on first launch. It is safe to continue: how to get past the SmartScreen prompt.

Docker

A headless image ships the CLI and the MCP server:

docker pull ghcr.io/thorstenfoltz/octa:latest

Mount a directory and pass any CLI flag:

docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/data" ghcr.io/thorstenfoltz/octa --schema /data/file.parquet

See the container docs for the MCP invocation and Podman.
